summary: Acme Insurance ran a security-focused review with Redwood to validate encryption in transit and at rest, KMS options (hosted keys vs BYOK), HSM support, key rotation, audit logs, and data residency. Redwood clarified the BYOK flow, envelope encryption, HSM-backed keys, and provided next steps to share certs, onboarding guides, and schedule a deeper technical session.
topics: Encryption at rest: SSE, envelope encryption, key rotation
KMS options: Redwood-managed, BYOK (customer KMS), HSM-backed keys
In-transit encryption: TLS, mutual TLS for private deployments
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. agenda is encryption, KMS/BYOK options, HSM questions, and next steps. quick intros?
[00:12] Jared Cole: Jared Cole, head of security at Acme. we run a hybrid cloud, lots of PHI-ish data, need strict residency and key control.
[00:22] Maya Singh: Maya, cloud infra; responsible for VPC, peering and network egress.
[00:29] Rafael Torres: Rafael, platform eng, will handle integration work.
[00:36] Alex Mercer: great. Samir, want to start on encryption at rest?
[00:40] Samir Patel: Sure—so by default Redwood encrypts data at rest with server-side encryption, envelope encryption using a master key. we also support customer-managed keys via BYOK and HSM-backed keys. note: some transcriptions may say K V cache, that's unrelated—sorry.
[01:05] Jared Cole: when you say envelope, does Redwood store the DEKs or only the encrypted blobs? who rotates keys?
[01:14] Samir Patel: good question. DEKs (data encryption keys) are generated per-asset and encrypted with the master KEK in KMS. if you're using Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood handles rotation and you get audit logs. with BYOK we still use envelope encryption but you hold the KEK in your KMS; Redwood can be granted decrypt/encrypt for wrapping via IAM, and you control rotation.
[01:36] Maya Singh: can you use HSM-backed keys in our cloud KMS? we require FIPS 140-2 level-3 equivalent.
[01:44] Samir Patel: yes, we integrate with cloud KMS providers that support HSM-backed keys (e.g., CloudKMS-HSM). for private/on-prem customers we also support connecting to customer HSMs via a mutual TLS gateway. small caveat: some on-prem HSMs need a dedicated network path and a maintenance window for key import.
[02:10] Rafael Torres: what's the BYOK flow—do we upload keys, or do you do key wrapping?
[02:16] Samir Patel: usually you create a key in your KMS and grant Redwood a wrapping/unwrapping role. Redwood never persists the plaintext key; we only store the wrapped DEKs. we provide an example policy (we'll share) that limits Redwood's actions to Encrypt/Decrypt for that key. for HSM import there is typically an import step—if you want keys fully generated in HSM you can do that and we reference them via key ARN.
[02:43] Jared Cole: how about key rotation—if we rotate the KEK, what happens to older DEKs?
[02:49] Samir Patel: DEKs stay encrypted with the KEK they were wrapped with; during rotation you can rewrap old DEKs with the new KEK via a backfill job or re-encrypt on access. Redwood supports automatic rewrap jobs or on-access rewrap depending on policy. we'll include recommended rotation cadence—commonly 90 days for KEK for high-sensitivity orgs.
[03:10] Alex Mercer: quick note—Acme's compliance ask: SOC2 and ISO27001 evidence, plus key custody. we'll get those certs out.
[03:18] Jared Cole: thanks. talking about audit logs—what's captured when keys are used? we need key usage logs for auditors.
[03:24] Lina Zhao: we surface key usage events in our audit logs: key encrypt/decrypt calls, who initiated (service principal or user), timestamp, and request metadata. you can export logs to your SIEM or a logging bucket. with BYOK, some of the lower-level HSM logs stay in your KMS and aren't forwarded, but we include our own access logs.
[03:48] Maya Singh: do we get immutable audit logs or will they be subject to retention policies? auditors require 3 years for certain records.
[03:56] Samir Patel: we offer configurable retention; default is 90 days in the Console but you can configure long-term export to your S3 or logging endpoint for indefinite retention. for enterprise customers we can provide longer retention and WORM storage options via your cloud account.
[04:15] Rafael Torres: network flow: if we pick BYOK, does Redwood need inbound access to our KMS? how does that work across VPC/private deploy?
[04:23] Samir Patel: For hosted mode, we authenticate to your KMS over the public control plane endpoints, using a least-privilege IAM principal. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we recommend peered VPCs or a private endpoint so traffic never leaves your network. for on-prem, we establish a mutual-TLS tunnel and you host KMS/HSM internally. we'll share a diagram.
[04:50] Jared Cole: data residency—we need tokens and data to remain in EU for certain workloads. can we pin region and ensure keys are EU-based?
[04:58] Lina Zhao: yes, we support region pinning at model/route level. for BYOK, keys should be created in the same region's KMS/HSM and we will never export them. we'll note that certain backups or metadata may still reside in control plane region unless you choose private control plane.
[05:20] Maya Singh: what about in transit? do you support mTLS between our services and Redwood?
[05:26] Samir Patel: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit by default. For Dedicated and Private we support mutual TLS and private networking options, plus IP allowlists and private peering.
[05:40] Alex Mercer: any limitations around tokenization or caching that impact encryption? Rafael mentioned KV cache earlier—clarify that please.
[05:47] Samir Patel: good callout. our KV cache is an in-memory runtime cache for model state (KV cache), but we do not persist sensitive prompt content to long-term storage unless configured. cached items in Dedicated instances are memory-resident on GPU nodes and cleared on eviction. if you need zero-cache persistence, we can toggle settings and isolate workload to nodes with no disk spill.
[06:18] Jared Cole: legal/contract question: do you support customer-managed HSM with import of key material vs. generate-in-HSM only? auditors ask for origin-of-key proofs.
[06:26] Samir Patel: depends on your KMS/HSM. Many cloud HSMs allow import of key material with provenance metadata; others require key generation inside the hardware. We can support either flow—if you need proof-of-origin (generated-in-HSM), we recommend generating the key in the HSM and sharing the key id/ARN. we'll document what auditors typically ask for.
[06:50] Maya Singh: what about rotation automation—can Redwood trigger rotation in our KMS, or do we manage that?
[06:57] Samir Patel: Typically customers manage KEK rotation in their KMS and Redwood uses the updated key. Redwood can optionally call a rotation API if you grant that permission; else you rotate and update permissions. We'll include both patterns in the guide.
[07:15] Rafael Torres: can you share an example IAM policy to grant minimal privileges?
[07:20] Lina Zhao: yes — sample policy allows Encrypt, Decrypt, and DescribeKey on the specific key ARN and denies broader actions. Samir will attach the snippet.
[07:30] Jared Cole: what about encryption of logs and backups? are backups encrypted with the same KEK?
[07:36] Samir Patel: backups—snapshot blobs are encrypted using envelope encryption; by default wrapped with the same KEK unless you specify a separate backup key. we can support per-backup key for extra segregation.
[07:50] Maya Singh: are there differences for embeddings vs generation outputs in storage? we store embeddings persistently for search—are those encrypted differently?
[07:58] Samir Patel: embeddings stored in our vector DB are encrypted at rest the same way. you can configure separate encryption policies per dataset if you want separation.
[08:12] Alex Mercer: cross-talk—sorry, quick Q: do you provide attestation for HSMs?
[08:17] Samir Patel: For certain HSM providers we can provide attestation documents; for in-house HSMs you can run an attestation challenge. We'll capture which attestation artifacts you need.
[08:30] Rafael Torres: latency concerns—wrapping/unwrapping on every request adds calls to KMS. does Redwood cache unwrapped keys in memory?
[08:38] Samir Patel: We never persist plaintext KEKs to disk. For performance we cache DEKs in memory per-node and keep KEK operations to minimal wrap/unwrap. Envelope encryption reduces KMS calls because DEKs handle bulk encryption. For high-throughput paths we also support tokenization and batching to reduce roundtrips. We'll share our performance profile.
[09:05] Jared Cole: about compliance—SOC2/ISO scope: does Redwood include Dedicated and Private in the scope?
[09:12] Lina Zhao: Our SOC2 and ISO reports cover our hosted control plane and hosted runtime; Dedicated clusters under Redwood-managed infrastructure are included per contract; Private deployments with self-managed control plane require a separate attestation depending on configuration. we'll clarify scope in the docs we send.
[09:34] Maya Singh: access control—SAML SSO, RBAC? we want role separation: platform ops vs devs.
[09:41] Samir Patel: we support SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. Roles can be scoped to projects, models, and routes. Audit trails show who invoked actions.
[09:57] Rafael Torres: can we rotate service principals and have Redwood pick up changes without downtime?
[10:03] Samir Patel: yes - we recommend dual credentials for rolling updates, and our clients support key rotation without dropping active requests. We'll provide a runbook.
[10:20] Alex Mercer: Jared—any specific red flags so far for Acme?
[10:24] Jared Cole: main concerns: custodial control over KEKs, HSM attestation, audit log retention, and ensuring EU residency for customer data. also want minimal attack surface for KMS integration.
[10:36] Alex Mercer: noted. Samir—any constraints on HSM vendors or import formats?
[10:42] Samir Patel: We generally work with standard cloud KMSs plus PKCS#11-compatible HSMs. For import, many HSMs accept wrapped key material using a standardized import token. We'll capture vendor-specific notes in the guide.
[10:58] Maya Singh: curious about failure modes—if KMS is unavailable, what happens to live inference?
[11:05] Samir Patel: Critical: if KEK unwrap fails, we cannot decrypt DEKs so access to persisted data fails. For active in-memory DEKs, runtime keeps serving until those DEKs expire. We recommend redundancy—multi-region KMS replication or a fallback key with strict controls. We'll show patterns for high availability.
[11:32] Rafael Torres: can we get per-request logs for key usage tied to request IDs for audit correlation?
[11:38] Lina Zhao: yes, our logs include request IDs and key usage events; you can correlate them in your SIEM. we'll include sample log schema.
[11:50] Alex Mercer: let's talk about the onboarding timeline briefly—pilot vs full rollout?
[11:55] Jared Cole: we'd like a small pilot with EU region, BYOK, and 30-day audit export.
[12:04] Samir Patel: sounds good — pilot plan: 2-week setup, run benchmarks, review key rotation and logs. we'll provide detailed steps.
[12:15] Maya Singh: any non-repudiation requirements? auditors ask for signed logs sometimes.
[12:20] Lina Zhao: we can support signed log exports using your KMS to sign log bundles before export; otherwise use your SIEM's signing. We'll add that option.
[12:35] Rafael Torres: can you confirm data deletion workflows—if we request data deletion, are wrapped DEKs deleted too?
[12:41] Samir Patel: Deletion flow: we can delete DEKs and blobs; for BYOK if you delete the KEK in your KMS, the wrapped DEKs become irrecoverable which is a viable native deletion. We'll include the deletion runbook.
[12:58] Alex Mercer: closing—recap and next steps?
[13:02] Alex Mercer: recap: Redwood supports envelope encryption, BYOK with minimal permissions, HSM-backed keys, audit exports, region pinning, mTLS for private deployments. deliverables: SOC2/ISO certs, BYOK/HSM guide, sample IAM policies, network diagram, schedule follow-up.
[13:20] Jared Cole: sounds right. thanks everyone.
[13:25] Alex Mercer: I'll send notes and docs after the call. we'll aim to get the pilot kickoff next week.
[13:32] Meeting ended
notes: Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and DPA
Provide sample IAM policy and BYOK onboarding guide
Discuss HSM attestation artifacts and import options
Configure log export to Acme SIEM for 3-year retention
